comments.body: I propose this Gloas-related issue https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/5735 for discussion

I'd like to propose discussing EIP-8365: the current spec skips deposits that would create new 0x00 validators, which burns the deposited ETH since the CL has no refund path, including valid pre-fork deposits still sitting in the deposit queue at the fork. 

Proposal: gate activation instead, so 0x00 deposits register with their full balance but are not activated until the holder changes credentials with `BLSToExecutionChange`. No ETH is burned, and the active 0x00 set still cannot grow.

- EIP change: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12513
- Spec change: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5744

I'd like ACDC to agree on this/some direction so the EF could publish a blog post officially announcing the plan and timeline now, giving 0x00 holders the longest possible notice to rotate.
 
1. Hegota: new 0x00 validators stop activating ([EIP-8365](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8365) + [PR 12513](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12513)). 
2. I fork: all remaining 0x00 validators are exited at the fork ([EIP-8433](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8433) + [PR 12514](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12514) ). No balance is touched, and rotating to 0x01 recovers it in full.
3. J fork: BLSToExecutionChange and the rest of the 0x00 code paths are removed ahead of the post-quantum transition, since the change message exposes the BLS withdrawal key. - still requires an EIP.

assuming a sucessful hoodi fork, I think we should aim to fork mainnet on
